artifact.split_description: temporal split on the VALIDATION instant, the shipped time column: train = appeals validated before 2020-01-01, eval = validated 2020-01-01..2021-12-31, holdout = validated on or after 2022-01-01. The candidate record's provisional partition was by decision year; the outcome date cannot ship (it is post-instant information) and the qualification gate requires disjoint split ranges on a shipped time column, so the split key moved to the instant - the same construction as the published ipo-trademark-registration-outcome (filed_date) and ec-merger-phase2-opening (notification_date) tasks. Slow cases mean a split's labels can postdate the next split's earliest instants; label timing is declared unverified and the artifact is retrospective research only.

data_compilation.scope: Our contribution - the s78_core eligibility frame (planning-permission-family casework with a binary Allowed/Dismissed decision), the counted exclusions (non-binary decisions, cross-file composite duplicates, decided-before-validation rows), the derived binary label from the publisher's Decision field, the derived date-gap and calendar features, the site-descriptor and designation flags, the LPA prior-outcome history features computed strictly from decisions earlier than the row's validation instant, the validation-instant temporal partition, and the packaging - is dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0. The dedication covers only our contribution: the underlying Planning Inspectorate Casework Database keeps its own designation and remains subject to the Open Government Licence v3.0, whose attribution condition carries through to every copy of the derived data. Nothing here relicenses the source or presents CC0 as the source's terms.

rules: Code and documentation: MIT by default.
Our rights in a derived compilation: CC0-1.0 by default.
The source's own terms are preserved and never relicensed; the compilation dedication covers only our contribution.

Each dataset must use terms compatible with its sources. CC0 is NOT a blanket override of upstream terms: attribution, share-alike and non-commercial requirements from a source are carried through unchanged.
A source whose licence terms cannot be read is not published at all.
The chosen terms are declared per dataset in candidates/<id>/license.json and recorded in the release manifest, so the manifest cannot drift from the decision.

source_data.status: Planning Inspectorate Casework Database (GOV.UK publication 'Planning Inspectorate Casework Database', 2026-10-22 edition) under the Open Government Licence v3.0: free to copy, publish, distribute, transmit, adapt and exploit commercially with the required attribution statement. OGL-UK exempts personal data, third-party rights and official symbols from its grant; the shipped columns were chosen with that in mind: the publisher's inspector-name field is excluded by design (post-instant and corrected for data errors by the publisher in 2025), no free-text applicant or site-occupier identity ships, and the LPA name/ONS code, casework type, procedure, development type, appeal reason fields, site descriptors and flags are redistributed exactly as the publisher publishes them, with nothing added beyond our derived binary label, the derived date/calendar features, the LPA prior-outcome history features, the eligibility frame, the deduplication and the partition. The derived dataset is labelled as such throughout and is not the Planning Inspectorate's official product. The publisher's own caveats carry through unchanged: some categorisation of appeals can be subjective; the data can change between different publications of this dataset; the extract covers decided cases only (in progress, withdrawn and turned away cases are not included); Local Plans Examination rows were removed by the publisher from the current Casework Database; TPO valid dates were removed by the publisher after a data-entry issue (TPO is out of this task's scope); and 'The Planning Inspectorate will not entertain a challenge to the appointment of any Decision Maker on the basis of this data.'

One model configuration, no re-tuning, two validation years of eval coverage - an observed result, not a bound on other models

population.censoring: none beyond the publisher's own decided-cases-only extract (in progress, withdrawn and turned away cases are not in the source); the outcome-conditioned population is a property of the publisher's database, recorded as a limitation
population.deduplication: cross-file dedup on (type, LPA, received, valid, decision date, decision): 3,110 rows appear in BOTH publisher files with identical composites (2021 decisions) and are deduplicated; counted, never silently dropped
population.eligibility: publisher Type of Casework in the s78_core family (e.g. Planning Appeal, Householder (HAS)); Decision in {Allowed, Dismissed}; Received/Valid/Decision dates parseable and decision not before validation
population.frame_fidelity: the in-build per-decision-year fixture reproduces the discovery probe exactly for all 11 decision years (kept + counted exclusions == probe n; kept_allowed + excluded_allowed == probe allowed); flag presence verified by direct letter-based counts
